newsitem.title: USA: Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer appoints movie unit chief.
newsitem.headline: Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer appoints movie unit chief.

text.p: Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Inc Wednesday named Robert Relyea to the newly created position of President - Production for MGM Pictures and United Artists Pictures, its two movie making divisions.

In a statement, MGM said Relyea, who has been executive vice president - production since 1993, will report to Robert Pisano, vice chairman. He has been part of the management team that helped boost MGM's film slate in 1996.
Upcoming films currently under Relyea's supervision include "Tomorrow Never Dies", the new movie based on fictional super spy, James Bond.
During his tenure at MGM, he has presided over the making of movies like "Get Shorty", "GoldenEye", and "The Birdcage".

Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer is co-owned by billionaire investor Kirk Kerkorian's Tracinda Corp and Australian media company Seven Network Ltd. Kerkorian also owns a controlling interest in hotel/casino operator MGM Grand Inc.
